about: Platform x feature matrix, hand-kept facts only (tools/parity/platforms.py renders it; the video rows come from data/caps.json and data/video.json instead). Each 'intel' fact cites the upstream line it was read from (trees in 'sources'); each 'ours' status is one of works / same / notyet / na and carries its evidence. No estimates: a platform nobody ran this driver on is 'notyet', whatever its code shares.

supported.about: The PCI devices (vendor 8086) this driver attaches to: the one list that every copy in the repository is checked against (tools/parity/devices.py; docs/design/DESIGN-platforms.md section 4). family: the kernel descriptor (kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp) that covers them, kernel_ids its id array. name: the card as messages name it; model: IntelXe.kext's 'model' property for it (the Metal device and the codecs take their names from it). tested: run on hardware by the project. gpu_test: what the app's GPU test (app/Sources/GPUTest.swift) expects of the card, generated into app/Sources/SupportedDevices.swift (python3 tools/parity/devices.py --write-swift): the FP32 compute rate in TFLOP/s and the VRAM copy bandwidth in GB/s it reaches (about), and the results at or above which the test says good / fair (below fair: bad); measured: false when the figures come from the specification, not from a run on the card; basis: where the figures come from.

gpu_test.basis: On the test machine, with the app's own kernels (fma16; copy4, VRAM to VRAM). The good and fair limits are the ones the app had before they moved here.

From Intel's specification of the B570: 18 Xe2-cores x 8 vector engines x 16 FP32 lanes = 2304 lanes, x 2 FLOP per FMA x 2500 MHz graphics clock = 11.52 TFLOP/s; 10 GB GDDR6 at 19 Gbps on a 160-bit bus = 19 x 160 / 8 = 380 GB/s (peak; a copy reaches less). The good/fair limits are the B580's scaled by the ratio of the two cards' specifications: compute 11.52 / 13.67 (B580: 20 Xe2-cores, 2670 MHz), memory 380 / 456 (B580: 192-bit, 19 Gbps).

From Intel's specification of the Arc Pro B60 (ark.intel.com product 243916: Device ID 0xE211, 20 Xe-cores, graphics clock 2400 MHz, 24 GB GDDR6, 192 bit, 19 Gbps, 456 GB/s): 20 Xe2-cores x 8 vector engines x 16 FP32 lanes = 2560 lanes, x 2 FLOP per FMA x 2400 MHz = 12.29 TFLOP/s; 456 GB/s peak (a copy reaches less). The good/fair limits are the B580's scaled by the ratio of the two cards' specifications: compute 12.29 / 13.67 (B580: 20 Xe2-cores, 2670 MHz), memory 456 / 456 (the B580's bus and memory speed).

From Intel's specification of the Arc Pro B50 (ark.intel.com product 242615: Device ID 0xE212, 16 Xe-cores, graphics clock 1700 MHz, max dynamic clock 2600 MHz, 16 GB GDDR6, 128 bit, 14 Gbps, 224 GB/s, 70 W): 16 Xe2-cores x 8 vector engines x 16 FP32 lanes = 2048 lanes, x 2 FLOP per FMA x 1700 MHz graphics clock = 6.96 TFLOP/s (the card draws only from the slot; Intel's graphics clock is used, as for the other cards); 224 GB/s peak (a copy reaches less). The good/fair limits are the B580's scaled by the ratio of the two cards' specifications: compute 6.96 / 13.67 (B580: 20 Xe2-cores, 2670 MHz), memory 224 / 456 (B580: 192-bit, 19 Gbps).

platforms.detail: the other IDs of Linux INTEL_BMG_IDS (kernel/IntelXe/xe_probe_ids.inc kIdsBMG: E202-E223): B570 = 8086:E20C, Pro B60 = 8086:E211, Pro B50 = 8086:E212 (BMG-G21), Pro B70 = 8086:E223 (BMG-G31; Intel product pages). IntelXe.kext attaches to 8086:E20B, since 0.1.4 to 8086:E20C, and since 2026-11-13 to 8086:E211 and E212 (kernel/IntelXe/build.py IOPCIMatch; all three untested on hardware); to BMG-G31 only with the tester boot-arg -intelxe_allow_g31.
